newsitem.title: USA: Soft Brent crude values deflate U.S. sweet grades.
newsitem.headline: Soft Brent crude values deflate U.S. sweet grades.

text.p: U.S. sweet crude grade prices deflated Wednesday morning on pressure from softer North Sea Brent CFD (Contract for Differences) values, traders said.
Benchmark September West Texas Intermediate/Cushing stood 10-15 cents lower at $20.60-70 a barrel, hurt by the seemingly imminent return of Iraqi crude exports and technical factors.
For the grades, Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James sold more than 10 cents weaker at a premiums of 13 and 15 cents to September WTI/Cushing.
Traders said the fact two Brent cargoes are fixed to the U.S. Gulf, and the 20 cents drop in Brent CFD's were the main reasons for the decline in LLS.
"Nobody bid it up this morning. You've got Dated Brent weaker and the Brent-WTI spread around $1.35, so that is working against the sweet," said a crude trader.
Other values saw West Texas Sour/Midland around a $1.40 discount to September WTI, and WTI/Cushing Postings Plus at $1.94-97, working off the September/October roll of -10/7 cents.
